hypotheses.justification: For every ε : ℝ≥0∞ we have 0 ≤ ε, so the set {x | ε < integralDensityLimsup μ f s x} is contained in {x | 0 < integralDensityLimsup μ f s x}, which is `integralDensitySet μ f s` by definition. That set has measure zero by `measure_integralDensitySet_eq_zero`. When ε = 0 the two sets are equal, so the excluded case also holds. Proof: replace `lt_trans hε hx` with `lt_of_le_of_lt (zero_le _) hx` (or `pos_of_gt hx`).

It is only passed to `measure_integralDensitySet_eq_zero`, which only passes it to `ae_integralDensityLimsup_eq_zero`. There the binder is `_hμ` and the proof (lines 93–150) never uses it: the proof only uses the doubling Vitali family, `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div`, `hf` and `hdim`. Without hμ, copy that proof body to get `∀ᵐ x ∂μ, integralDensityLimsup μ f s x = 0`. Then finish as now with `measure_mono_null` (from ε < L x we get L x ≠ 0).

Like hμ, it only reaches `ae_integralDensityLimsup_eq_zero`, where it is the unused binder `_hs`. That proof only divides by `ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ s)`. In ℝ≥0∞, monotonicity of division (`gcongr`) and `ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul` hold for any denominator, so nothing needs s ≥ 0. The statement holds for negative s by the same argument: inline that proof without hs, then apply `measure_mono_null` as before.
